[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Instruction Tuning and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) in Natural Language Processing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Instruction tuning and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) are pivotal paradigms in modern Natural Language Processing (NLP). While base Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at next-token prediction over vast web corpora, they often struggle to follow explicit user instructions out of the box. SFT bridges this gap by training pre-trained models on curated datasets of instruction-response pairs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the SFT Pipeline"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The SFT process transforms an unsupervised base model into a helpful assistant. The dataset typically consists of prompts and corresponding desired outputs. During training, the model computes the loss only on the response tokens while masking the prompt tokens, ensuring it learns to generate accurate continuations rather than predicting the user's prompt."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Base Model: A model trained purely on causal language modeling (autoregressive prediction)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dataset Construction: High-quality pairs of prompts and gold-standard responses."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Loss Masking: Applying cross-entropy loss exclusively on the completion tokens."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing SFT with Hugging Face and PyTorch"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a practical code snippet utilizing the Hugging Face transformers and trl libraries to perform Supervised Fine-Tuning efficiently."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainingArguments
from trl import SFTTrainer
from datasets import load_dataset

model_id = "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, load_in_4bit=True, device_map="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

dataset = load_dataset("databricks/databricks-dolly-15k", split="train[:1000]")

training_args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="./sft_results",
    per_device_train_batch_size=4,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=4,
    learning_rate=2e-5,
    logging_steps=10,
    max_steps=100,
    fp16=True
)

trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    dataset_text_field="text",
    max_seq_length=512,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    args=training_args,
)

trainer.train()"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Instruction Tuning"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Quality over Quantity: A few thousand diverse, high-quality instruction pairs often outperform millions of noisy examples."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prompt Formatting: Maintain a consistent template (e.g., Alpaca or ChatML format) across training and inference."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT): Utilize methods like LoRA or QLoRA to reduce memory overhead during training."}]
